title: Herbicide to Rough, Handgun
sheet_name: Herbicides to Rough - Handgun (1000L Silvan - 600L/Ha - Handgun)
checks: Tank, hose and gun rinsed since the last load
Residue in the hose can damage the next job
Suction and gun filters clean, lid seal good
Hose and reel: no cracks, kinks or leaks
Gun trigger, lock and nozzle work, no drips
Gun output: spray into a bucket for 30 s, double it for L/min
600 L/ha is 6 L per 10 × 10 m. At 12 L/min that's 30 s per 10 × 10 m
Fill hose above the water line
Spill kit, wash water and eyewash on the rig
Labels and SDSs for all 8 products with you
Spray signs out where you're working
Wind 3–20 km/h (Tri-Kombi label) · not gusting toward greens or tees
extra_checks: Spraying well clear of greens, collars and tees
Firepower and Fusilade kill bent and most grasses

products.note: Goes in 2nd (sheet has it 6th): the suspension goes in before the oils and ECs.

ppe_note: Tri-Kombi's label asks for a half-face respirator with organic vapour cartridges and a chemical-resistant suit when mixing and when spraying by hand. Face shield when pouring Firepower and Fusilade.
spray_rules: Broadleaf weeds and the rough the boom can't reach only. Wet the leaf until the dye shows, not to run-off
Stay well clear of greens, collars and tees. Firepower and Fusilade kill bent and most grasses
Wind 3–20 km/h. Stop when it gusts toward a green, tee, garden bed or the boundary. Keep the gun low and the spray coarse
Lock the gun when you move the hose, and keep the hose off greens and tees
Keep people off until it's dry. Write down where you sprayed: no mowing there for 2 days and no irrigation tonight
spray_more: Tri-Kombi label: wind 3–20 km/h, no spraying in a surface inversion, no heavy rain or storms within 3 days, don't mow 2 days before or after, don't irrigate to run-off for 3 days, not by backpack sprayer. Quinstar: avoid irrigation within 8 h. Fusilade: rainfast in 1 h.
post_checks: Tank sprayed out on the target rough
Hose and gun flushed with clean water
Sprayed out on the rough you treated
Suit, gloves, goggles and face shield washed. Respirator wiped, cartridges sealed in a bag
So the rough mowing (not before Wed 21 Oct) and tonight's irrigation can skip them
post_fields: e.g. 14 rough left of the fairway, under the trees on 3

flags.t: Methar Tri-Kombi 4.5 L/ha is over its label maximum
flags.d: Label rate for golf fairways, parks and lawns is 4.2 L in 450 L water per ha, and 4.2 L/ha is the stated maximum. This tank has 7.5 L; at the label max it would be 7.0 L. Victoria allows off-label use at or below the label rate, not above it. Built as the sheet stands (Andy, 19 Oct).

flags.t: Sportsground + Tri-Kombi: the same three-way twice
flags.d: Both are Campbell three-ways with mecoprop 336 + dicamba 40 g/L. At 4.5 L/ha each that's about 3.0 kg/ha mecoprop and 360 g/ha dicamba, against 1.4 kg/ha and 168 g/ha at Tri-Kombi's label maximum. Sportsground's registered label (APVMA 31538) wasn't readable online; the retailer lists its third active as MCPA 80 g/L.
flags.s: APVMA 31536 label · Pestrol and HerbiGuide listings

flags.t: Two Group 1 grass herbicides, neither registered on turf
flags.d: Firepower 900 is haloxyfop-R 900 g/L (90 g/ha here), registered for forestry and industrial grass control. Fusilade Forte is fluazifop-P 128 g/L (192 g/ha here), registered for horticulture, ornamentals and plantations. Both are off-label on turf: Victoria allows that at or below label rates. Same mode of action, so the second adds little over the first.
flags.s: ADAMA Firepower tech note and SDS · Fusilade Forte label APVMA 58521

flags.t: Fusilade label: no tank mixes without Syngenta
flags.d: The label says DO NOT tank mix with other pesticides without prior reference to a Syngenta representative. It also says no adjuvant is needed.

flags.t: Hormones knock back Group 1 activity on kikuyu
flags.d: Phenoxy and dicamba herbicides antagonise haloxyfop and fluazifop on grasses: the same issue flagged on the earlier rough mix. If kikuyu is a real target, a separate Group 1 tank (with Hasten) would work better than this one.
flags.s: Known antagonism, previous rough mix review

flags.d: Haloxyfop and fluazifop kill bent, couch and kikuyu, and neither label lists fescue as tolerant. Quinstar lists couch, zoysia, ryegrass, Kentucky bluegrass and bent as tolerant, not tall fescue; on kikuyu it's suppression only (2 applications 14–21 days apart, autumn best). The retailer listing for Sportsground says avoid kikuyu and Qld blue couch.

Tri-Kombi's label: half-face respirator with organic vapour cartridges when opening and mixing and when spraying by hand, chemical-resistant clothing, washable hat, elbow-length gloves, impervious footwear and goggles for mixing. Fusilade: face shield and elbow-length PVC gloves.

Hasten's label says add it last and keep agitating. Quinstar (a suspension concentrate) goes in 2nd so it disperses before the oils (Firepower, Fusilade) and the amine salts (Sportsground, Tri-Kombi). Rates are as the sheet.
Morning brief: N 12–15 km/h with gusts 28–29 km/h from 11am to 1pm, easing to 26 by 6pm, 27 °C. Tri-Kombi's limit is 3–20 km/h. Spray the lulls and stop when it gusts toward anything that matters.

Tri-Kombi and Quinstar: don't mow 2 days before or after. Quinstar: avoid irrigation within 8 h. Tri-Kombi: don't irrigate to run-off for 3 days. The post-application checklist asks for the areas sprayed so the rough mowing and the night irrigation can skip them.
